exemplars.title: DNS and TLS diagnostic CLI
exemplars.scenario: A small support team gets intermittent “site unavailable” reports. Build a safe diagnostic that separates resolver, TCP, HTTP, and certificate symptoms. Linux/macOS terminal, Python 3, Git; network tests only to an explicitly approved target. Never collect cookies, auth headers, or private key material.
exemplars.starter_tree:
levels/01-operator-foundations/exemplar/01-dns-tls-diagnostics/
├── README.md  Makefile  .gitignore
├── src/diagnose.py
├── fixtures/dns-ok.txt fixtures/dns-nxdomain.txt fixtures/tls-ok.txt fixtures/tls-expired.txt
├── tests/test_diagnose.py
├── docs/adr/0001-diagnostic-boundaries.md docs/runbook.md REPORT.md
└── scripts/validate.sh
tasks: Implement `python -m src.diagnose --target example.test --fixture-dir fixtures --json`; fixture mode must not access the network.
Optional `--live` requires explicit allowlisted hostname and bounded timeout.
Use `dig`/`getent` and `curl`/`openssl` only in live mode; classify each layer and redact target credentials/query strings.
Add a Git commit sequence demonstrating tests before the feature and an ADR explaining why fixture mode is default.

steps: Substitute the NXDOMAIN fixture, then the expired-certificate fixture.
Confirm the tool distinguishes DNS from TLS, returns nonzero for a failed diagnostic, and does not emit secrets.
Restore the passing fixture.

deliverables: REPORT with sample terminal output and limitations
validation_and_acceptance: `make validate` runs formatting/compile checks and `python -m unittest discover -s tests -v`.
Tests assert stable JSON keys, error classifications, bounded timeout configuration, correct exit codes, and redaction.
`make validate` must pass offline; malformed fixtures must fail safely, not crash with a traceback.
exemplars.acceptance: A reviewer can clone and run tests without credentials; the two injected faults produce distinct, reproducible diagnoses.
cost_controls_and_cleanup: No cloud resources.
Remove temp files; `git status --short` is clean except intentional source/docs.
Live targets are allowlisted and opt-in.

exemplars.title: Safe AWS S3 inventory (read-only)
exemplars.scenario: An auditor needs a concise inventory of a designated sandbox bucket's public-access block, encryption, versioning, and lifecycle posture. No object bodies, no writes, no bucket creation by default. AWS CLI profile and region must be explicitly supplied; only a sandbox allowlisted bucket is eligible for optional live mode.
exemplars.starter_tree:
levels/02-aws-foundations/exemplar/01-safe-s3-inventory/
├── README.md Makefile config/allowlist.json
├── src/audit.py scripts/preflight.sh
├── fixtures/bucket-good.json fixtures/bucket-risky.json
├── tests/test_audit.py tests/test_preflight.py
└── docs/adr/0001-read-only-inventory.md docs/runbook.md REPORT.md
tasks: `scripts/preflight.sh PROFILE REGION` checks `aws sts get-caller-identity`, exact approved account placeholder from local config, region allowlist, and explicit bucket allowlist before any API calls.
`python -m src.audit --fixture fixtures/bucket-risky.json --json` produces deterministic findings.

Live mode invokes only read APIs (`get-public-access-block`, `get-bucket-encryption`, `get-bucket-versioning`, `get-bucket-lifecycle-configuration`); handle absent configuration separately from AccessDenied.
Never infer public access solely from one setting.

steps: Change active profile or region in a test stub and prove preflight blocks live mode.
Use the risky fixture and confirm findings include remediation and evidence source.
Simulate AccessDenied; report “unknown,” not “secure.”

validation_and_acceptance: `make validate` runs unit tests against checked-in JSON and asserts zero write API names in the command allowlist, stable JSON ordering, fail-closed identity, and correct distinction among compliant, misconfigured, and unknown.
Optional `make integration` requires explicit environment confirmation and emits no object contents.
exemplars.acceptance: Wrong identity prevents all API operations; offline tests work with no AWS credentials.
cost_controls_and_cleanup: Default lab is read-only and has no resource creation.
If a dedicated test bucket is authorized separately, Terraform owns it; apply only after review, use tags/TTL, and destroy plus list-bucket verification.
No public ACL/policy.

exemplars.title: Container to repeatable delivery pipeline
exemplars.scenario: A two-person team must ship a tiny HTTP health service consistently. Build locally first; optional AWS deploy is out of scope. Image runs non-root, has no embedded secrets, and can be rolled back by immutable digest.
exemplars.starter_tree:
levels/03-repeatable-delivery/exemplar/01-container-to-pipeline/
├── app/server.py app/requirements.txt
├── Dockerfile .dockerignore Makefile
├── tests/test_health.py scripts/build-test.sh scripts/promote.sh
├── .github/workflows/ci.yml release/manifest.schema.json
└── docs/adr/0001-immutable-artifacts.md docs/runbook.md REPORT.md
tasks: Implement `/healthz`; use a pinned base image tag/digest policy, non-root user, minimal build context, deterministic unit tests, image build, container smoke test, and digest-based release manifest.
CI runs tests, image build, config checks, and secret scan.
Promotion copies the digest into a release manifest; it must not rebuild.

failure_drill.restore_baseline: Restore source and confirm previous known-good digest remains usable.
steps: Make health check fail and verify the deploy/smoke script refuses promotion.
Modify a manifest digest and prove integrity validation fails.
Restore source and confirm previous known-good digest remains usable.

validation_and_acceptance: `make validate` runs unit tests, Dockerfile/pipeline static checks, build and smoke test when Docker is available; a no-Docker unit target is documented.
Assertions: non-root user, health endpoint responds, no `.env`/credentials in build context, failed health prevents promotion, digest unchanged between environments.
exemplars.acceptance: Clean checkout test/build path works and injected unhealthy image cannot be promoted.
cost_controls_and_cleanup: Local images/containers only; `make clean` stops/removes named lab container and image.
Verify no running container remains.
CI uses no paid cloud runner assumption; do not commit secrets.

exemplars.title: SLO and failure drill with synthetic telemetry
exemplars.scenario: An API owner has synthetic request records and wants a user-facing availability/latency SLO, a useful alert, and a blameless incident report. No live monitoring deployment. Dataset is synthetic and time-bounded.
exemplars.starter_tree:
levels/04-reliability-operations/exemplar/01-slo-failure-drill/
├── data/requests.csv data/alerts.json
├── src/slo.py src/timeline.py tests/test_slo.py tests/test_timeline.py
├── scripts/inject_failure.py Makefile
└── docs/slo.md docs/runbook.md docs/incident-report.md REPORT.md
tasks: Calculate request-based availability and p95 latency by fixed window, document denominator/exclusions, and calculate remaining error budget from an explicitly declared target in `docs/slo.md`.
Generate a timeline from UTC event fixtures.
Alert rule must identify customer symptom, owner, threshold rationale, and runbook.
Do not claim SLO targets as industry standards; label them as exercise assumptions.

steps: `python scripts/inject_failure.py --profile elevated-5xx --output /tmp/requests.csv` adds a deterministic burst; show SLI/error-budget change and produce a timeline.
Then inject missing timestamps and verify they are counted/reported rather than silently discarded.

validation_and_acceptance: `make validate` tests fixed expected counts, percentile convention, empty windows, timezone handling, malformed data, and deterministic output.
Failure dataset must breach the exercise threshold; baseline must not.
Report contains impact, timeline, detection, response, recovery, contributing factors, and owned follow-ups.
exemplars.acceptance: Baseline and injected-failure outputs are reproducible from a fresh checkout.
cost_controls_and_cleanup: Local fixtures only; remove temp outputs with `make clean`.
No cloud service is created.

exemplars.title: Least-privilege S3 data path
exemplars.scenario: A batch role reads and writes only its own synthetic prefix in an approved sandbox bucket. The lab teaches policy design, not production key administration. No public access; no real data; live apply requires reviewed sandbox account and budget controls.
exemplars.starter_tree:
levels/05-cloud-security/exemplar/01-least-privilege-data-path/
├── infra/main.tf infra/variables.tf infra/outputs.tf
├── policies/batch-role.json policy-tests/matrix.yaml
├── scripts/check_policy.py tests/test_policy.py
└── docs/threat-model.md docs/adr/0001-data-access.md docs/runbook.md REPORT.md
tasks: Define a Terraform-managed private bucket with encryption and public-access blocks, plus a role policy scoped to the named bucket prefix and required actions only.
Write an authorization matrix of allowed and denied actions/resources.
Keep state remote-backend configuration as a documented example, not a hard-coded backend with learner credentials.
Run static policy tests before any optional apply.

steps: Inject `Resource: "*"` or an extra destructive action into a policy fixture.
Validation must fail and show which matrix case violates the boundary.
Restore the least-privilege policy.
In optional sandbox mode, test denied access using a separate test principal only if explicitly authorized; never use production identities.

validation_and_acceptance: `make validate` runs Terraform fmt/validate, plan/policy static checks, and Python matrix tests; no credentials required.
Assert public access blocked, encryption configured, actions/resources constrained, all deny cases remain denied.
Live mode requires preflight, reviewed plan, TTL, and explicit confirmation.
exemplars.acceptance: Wildcard injection fails before apply; no secrets/state are committed.
cost_controls_and_cleanup: Plan-only by default.
If applied, use Terraform destroy, then independently query bucket/object versions and IAM attachments; empty versioned contents via a separately reviewed cleanup script before destroy.
Record cleanup proof.
Do not delete resources not created by this lab.

exemplars.title: Resilient service architecture decision
exemplars.scenario: A fictional order API must tolerate one-zone impairment, meet an exercise-defined recovery objective, and operate with a small team. Workload and traffic figures are invented exercise inputs, clearly labeled; no live service is required.
exemplars.starter_tree:
levels/06-architecture-decisions/exemplar/01-resilient-service-design/
├── requirements/brief.md requirements/assumptions.yaml
├── src/failure_model.py src/cost_model.py tests/
├── diagrams/architecture.mmd docs/adr/0001-topology.md
└── docs/review.md docs/runbook.md REPORT.md
tasks: Extract functional/NFR requirements and unresolved assumptions; compare at least two topologies; model dependency and failure-domain propagation; diagram identity, data, network, and observability flows; state RTO/RPO, recovery steps, and cost drivers.
The model is a decision aid, not a reliability prediction.
Include trigger conditions to revisit the ADR.

steps: Mark one zone unavailable and then make the shared database dependency unavailable.
Verify the model shows the first recovery path and the second as a hard limit; revise the design or explicitly accept the gap.
Do not represent unmodeled services as highly available.

validation_and_acceptance: `make validate` validates requirements/ADR metadata, diagram source presence, and deterministic failure-model fixtures.
Tests assert declared objectives against exercise scenarios, identify single points of failure, and reject unknown dependency ownership.
Review checklist includes tradeoffs and residual risks.
exemplars.acceptance: Reviewer can change a stated assumption and see which recommendation or risk changes.
cost_controls_and_cleanup: No cloud deployment.
If the learner adds an optional Terraform proof, it must be separately scoped, low-cost, plan-reviewed, tagged, time-limited, and destroyed with inventory verification.

exemplars.title: Guardrailed golden path
exemplars.scenario: A platform team wants a repeatable starter for small internal APIs. It must make safe defaults easy, permit documented exceptions, and keep validation local. No organization-wide policy or account vending apply.
tasks: `new-service.sh NAME` safely creates a starter from a template; validate input and refuse overwrite.
Template includes health check, non-root container, tests, CI, runbook, ownership, and Terraform module interface.
Policy tests check region, tags, encryption, and no public exposure.
Exceptions require owner, rationale, compensating control, expiry, and review date.

steps: Generate a service with an invalid name, attempt overwrite, introduce a public ingress fixture, and add an expired exception.
Each must fail with actionable output before cloud calls.

validation_and_acceptance: `make validate` generates a temp service, runs its tests, checks generated files, runs policy fixtures, verifies idempotent behavior, and cleans temp dirs.
Passing and failing fixtures cover each rule.
No cloud credential is needed.
exemplars.acceptance: One command creates a working safe starter; violations fail closed with a fix hint.
cost_controls_and_cleanup: Local-only.
Optional Terraform example is plan-only; any live test uses sandbox preflight, budget notification, TTL tags, and verified destroy.
Never run generated infrastructure automatically as part of `new-service.sh`.

exemplars.title: Provider capability and hybrid decision map
exemplars.scenario: A fictional enterprise is evaluating whether one new workload should stay on AWS, use GCP, use Azure, or connect to an on-prem dependency. Focus on identity, network, governance, logging, key management, data transfer, and exit strategy. No provider resources are created by default.
exemplars.starter_tree:
levels/08-clouds-hybrid/exemplar/01-provider-capability-map/
├── data/capabilities.yaml data/assumptions.yaml
├── scripts/validate_matrix.py scripts/preflight-aws.sh scripts/preflight-gcp.sh scripts/preflight-azure.sh
├── infra/aws/ infra/gcp/ infra/azure/ (plan-only examples)
└── docs/mapping.md docs/adr/0001-provider-choice.md docs/runbook.md REPORT.md
tasks: Build a sourced capability matrix across AWS IAM/VPC/CloudTrail/KMS, GCP IAM/VPC/Audit Logs/Cloud KMS, and Azure Entra ID/VNet/Activity Logs/Key Vault, noting scope and non-equivalence rather than claiming universal parity.
Use Terraform provider-specific examples and CLI preflights (`aws sts`, `gcloud auth list`/project, `az account show`) that fail closed on unexpected identity/project/subscription.
Record verification date/source for mutable capabilities and treat CLI output as sensitive metadata.

steps: Feed each preflight a wrong identity/project/subscription fixture and prove it blocks before Terraform apply.
Inject a false “equivalent” matrix row; schema validation must require a caveat/evidence field.
Simulate hybrid DNS forwarding failure in local fixtures and document the boundary.

validation_and_acceptance: `make validate` checks YAML schema, required evidence fields, deterministic scoring inputs, and Terraform formatting/validation where providers are available.
Offline mode requires no login.
Each cloud's live plan is separate, opt-in, region-scoped, and never applied by the default target.
exemplars.acceptance: Recommendation names provider-specific dependencies, operational burden, portability limits, and conditions that would change the choice.
cost_controls_and_cleanup: Default no resources.
Any optional proof uses one provider at a time, dedicated sandbox, budget alert, TTL, provider preflight, and exact Terraform destroy plus provider CLI inventory check.
Avoid cross-cloud data transfer during testing.

exemplars.title: Design review and crisis response
exemplars.scenario: You are the architecture lead for a fictional checkout service. Reviewers dispute the proposed migration, then a simulated regional impairment occurs during cutover. There is no real customer or cloud system. Communicate for engineers, incident responders, and executives.
exemplars.starter_tree:
levels/09-architecture-leadership/exemplar/01-review-and-crisis/
├── review/brief.md review/options.yaml review/agenda.md
├── incident/events.yaml scripts/tabletop.py scripts/check_actions.py
├── docs/adr/0001-cutover-strategy.md docs/incident-report.md
└── docs/executive-brief.md portfolio/evidence-index.md REPORT.md
tasks: Prepare a time-boxed review agenda, requirements/assumptions, options, decision criteria, dissent log, and go/no-go gates.
Execute a terminal tabletop that advances synthetic events and requires role, decision, owner, next update, and evidence for each action.
Produce a concise executive brief with impact, recommendation, tradeoff, uncertainty, and decision requested.
Avoid invented customer impact or financial figures: use scenario data and label it.

steps: Inject conflicting telemetry and a missed cutover readiness gate.
Operator must pause or roll back according to declared criteria, state what is known/unknown, assign incident roles, and issue the next update.
Then run the post-incident action linter against one vague corrective action and improve it to have owner, due date, verification, and priority.

validation_and_acceptance: `make validate` checks required review/ADR/report fields, verifies every action has owner/verification, confirms a failed readiness gate blocks cutover, and checks evidence links resolve locally.
Tabletop transcript must contain timeline, decision rationale, recovery signal, and customer-safe update.
Executive brief stays within the exercise's one-page/word-limit rule.
exemplars.acceptance: A second person can run the tabletop and reach the same declared go/no-go outcome from the evidence.
cost_controls_and_cleanup: No cloud resources; delete generated temporary event transcripts if they contain sensitive practice notes.
Public portfolio uses synthetic names only.
